messages.subject: two level mediation model
parts:
Dear Stan users, 

I am working on a two-level longitudinal mediation model. Here is the model
Level 1 complete mediation model

 M_t=mM_t-1+a(t) X_t-1+error
Y_t=yY_t-1+b(t)M_t-1+error

Level 2 AR(1) model

a(t)=mu1+alpha*[a(t-1)-mu1]+error
b(t)=mu_2+alpha[b(t-1)-mu2]+error

The following is my code to simulate data and run rstan

###simulate data
N=500
T=100
TS1=c()
TS2=c()

  TS1[1]= 0.4+0.5*(rnorm(1, 0.4, 0.05)-0.4)+rnorm(1, 0, sqrt(0.003))
  TS2[1]= 0.5+0.4*(rnorm(1, 0.5, 0.05)-0.5)+rnorm(1, 0, sqrt(0.003))
  for(j in 2:(T+5000)){
    TS1[j]= 0.4+0.5*(TS1[j-1]-0.4)+rnorm(1, 0, sqrt(0.003))
    TS2[j]= 0.5+0.4*(TS2[j-1]-0.5)+rnorm(1, 0, sqrt(0.003))
  }

##compute M and Y

X<-matrix(NA,nrow=N, ncol=(5000+T))##burn out 5000
M<-matrix(NA,nrow=N, ncol=(5000+T))
Y<-matrix(NA,nrow=N, ncol=(5000+T))

for(i in 1:N){
  X[i, 1]=rnorm(1, 0, 0.140)
  M[i, 1]=rnorm(1, 0, 2.58)
  Y[i, 1]=rnorm(1, 0, 4.08)
  for(t in 2:(T+5000)){
    X[i, t]=0.7*X[i, t-1]+rnorm(1)
  ##compute Mediator
  M[i, t]=0.6*M[i, t-1]+TS1[t]*X[i,t-1 ]+rnorm(1)
  ##compute Y
  
  Y[i, t]=0.8*Y[i, t-1]+TS2[t]*M[i, t-1]+rnorm(1)
  }
}
X=X[,-(1:5000)]##500 by 100
Y=Y[, -(1:5000)]##500 by 100
M=M[, -(1:5000)]##500 by 100


###stan

tsmod<-"
data{
int<lower=0> N;
      int<lower=0> T;
matrix[N,T] X;
matrix[N,T] Y;
      matrix[N,T] M;
}

parameters {
    real<lower=-0.8, upper=0.8> mu1;
    real<lower=-0.8, upper=0.8> mu2; 
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> x;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> y;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> m;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> a;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> b;
    real<lower=0> VY;
    real<lower=0> VX;
    real<lower=0> VM;
    real<lower=0> v1;
    real<lower=0> v2;  
   }

model{
   matrix[N, T] UX; 
   matrix[N, T] UY;
   matrix[N, T] UM;
   vector[N] UX0;
   vector[N] UM0;
   vector[N] UY0;
vector[T] TS1;
vector[T] TS2;
vector[T] U1;
vector[T] U2;
vector[2] TS0;
  for( i in 1 : N ) {
    X[i, 1]~normal(UX[i, 1], VX);
    M[i, 1]~normal(UM[i, 1], VM);
    Y[i, 1]~normal(UY[i, 1], VY);
    UX[i, 1]<-x*UX0[i];
    UM[i, 1]<-m*UM0[i]+TS1[1]*UX0[i];
    UY[i, 1]<-y*UY0[i]+TS2[1]*UM0[i];
    UX0[i]~normal(0, 2);
    UM0[i]~normal(0, 6);
    UY0[i]~normal(0, 16);
    for(t in 2:T){
      X[i, t]~normal(UX[i,t], VX);
      Y[i, t] ~normal(UY[i,t], VY);
      M[i,t]~normal(UM[i, t], VM);
      UX[i, t]<-x*X[i, t-1];
      UM[i,t]<-m*M[i, t-1]+TS1[t]*X[i, t];
      UY[i,t]<-y*Y[i, t]+TS2[t]*M[i, t];
    }}
  
  for(t in 2: T){
    TS1[t]~normal(U1[t], v1);
    TS2[t]~normal(U2[t], v2);
    U1[t]<-mu1+a*(TS1[t-1]-mu1);
    U2[t]<-mu2+b*(TS2[t-1]-mu2);
  }
  
  TS1[1]~normal(U1[1], v1);
  TS2[1]~normal(U2[1], v2);
  U1[1]<-mu1+a*(TS0[1]-mu1);
  U2[1]<-mu2+b*(TS0[2]-mu2);  
  TS0[1]~normal(0,0.003);
  TS0[2]~normal(0,0.003);
  VX~inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  VY~inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  VM~inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  v1~inv_gamma(100, 0.01);
  v2~inv_gamma(100, 0.01);
  x~uniform(-1, 1);
  y~uniform(-1, 1);
  m~uniform(-1, 1);
  a~uniform(-1, 1);
  b~uniform(-1, 1);
  mu1~uniform(-0.8, 0.8);
  mu2~uniform(-0.8, 0.8);
}
"

##inits
inits<-list(list(mu1=0.4, mu2=0.5, x=0.7, y=0.8, m=0.6, a=0.5, b=0.4, VX=1, VY=1, VM=1, v1=0.003,v2=0.003))

data <- list (N=500, T=100, X=as.matrix(X), M=as.matrix(M), Y=as.matrix(Y))

output<-stan(model_code = tsmod, data = data, init = inits, chains = 1,iter = 5000,
  verbose = TRUE, include = TRUE)


This is the error message from rstan is as follows:


SAMPLING FOR MODEL '1898e6e3c0967b07eafe1a3c3a482b02' NOW (CHAIN 1).
[1] "Error : "                                                                                                                              
[2] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[3] "Exception thrown at line 39: stan::math::normal_log: Location parameter is 1.#QNAN, but must be finite!"                               
[4] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[5] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                              
[6] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[7] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                          
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

Ｉam a brand new user. I would be very grateful if someone can help me out.

Thanks
Haiyan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] two level mediation model
parts:
You're using a variable in a sampling statement before
it's defined. Stan's sampling statements (the ones with ~)
are just syntactic sugar for incrementing the log density, so
all the terms need to be defined. Parameters and data
will be defined from the outside, but local variables,
transformed data, and transformed parameters must all be
defined in the program before being used.

If they're unknowns, then you'll want to make them parameters.

- Bob
